description:
Redwood Inference is refreshing its developer-facing examples across SDKs and documentation to reflect the current best-practice interface for (1) streaming responses, (2) function/tool calling, and (3) structured output/JSON schema. The goal is to eliminate inconsistency across Python/TypeScript/Go, reduce support load from confusing or outdated snippets, and improve time-to-first-success for PLG users building agentic workflows.

Goals:
- Provide a single, consistent mental model for streaming across languages (event types, partial deltas, final message assembly, error handling).
- Update tool-calling examples to match Redwood’s supported semantics (tool definitions, arguments validation, parallel tool calls, tool-result messages).
- Add structured output examples that demonstrate JSON schema constraints and robust parsing/validation.
- Improve documentation/quickstarts so that “copy/paste” examples work end-to-end and are versioned/maintained.

Scope:
- SDKs: redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript, redwood-sdk-go (examples + tests + any small ergonomic fixes).
- Docs: redwood-docs (API reference pages + guides), Confluence DX standards, and redwood-quickstarts templates.
- Examples: redwood-examples repo (small runnable samples + README alignment).
- Support feedback loop: synthesize recent tickets and Solutions Engineering notes into a “known pitfalls” section.

Non-goals:
- Major API redesign of streaming/tool calling protocols.
- Large product feature work beyond small SDK-level ergonomics and documentation clarifications.

Stakeholders:
- Executive sponsor: Alex Martinez (VP Developer Experience).
- SDK ownership: Monica Patel (Director, SDK Engineering) with Ibrahim Khan (Staff SWE, SDKs), Dana Lo (TS SDK), Mateusz Zielinski (Go SDK).
- Docs ownership: Elliot Price (Director, Technical Documentation) with Wei Chen (Hosted API docs).
- Product partner: Nikhil Sharma (Director of Product, Hosted API) and Henry Cho (Sr PM).
- Field/support input: Markus Klein (Director, Solutions Engineering) and Dev Patel (Director, Customer Support).

Phases & timeline (typical 4–6 weeks):
1) Audit & parity matrix (week 1): identify mismatches in streaming/tool-call examples across languages/docs; gather top support pain.
2) Spec & standards (week 1–2): lock event nomenclature, example conventions, structured-output schema guidance; write internal standard pages.
3) Implementation (week 2–4): PRs to SDKs, docs site, and examples/quickstarts; add tests (“golden” transcripts) for streaming tool calls.
4) Review & rollout (week 4–6): cross-language review, docs publish, changelog/release notes, support enablement, and follow-up tickets.

Constraints and risks:
- Backwards compatibility: examples must not require unreleased SDK APIs; where behavior differs by version, docs must call it out.
- Model variability: tool calling and JSON-structured output can differ across models; examples should include guidance and fallbacks.
- Streaming edge cases: disconnect/retry semantics, partial tool-call arguments, and incremental JSON need careful handling and tests.

Key deliverables:
- Updated streaming + tool calling + structured output examples in Python/TS/Go.
- Updated quickstarts/templates and docs pages that align to the same canonical patterns.
- Internal Confluence “DX standards” pages describing how examples should be written and tested.
- Linear-tracked work breakdown + a small set of Jira-linked learnings from support cases.
